headline: Medical Microinstruments, a Florida maker of surgical robots, has raised $125 million to sell its microsurgery robot more widely.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct and confirmed by the company, but it is a funding round, not a new capability.
importance_line: Surgeons and patients needing delicate vessel or nerve repair may get wider access to a robot-assisted option, while its use in Alzheimer's patients is only being tested for safety so far.
summary: Medical Device Network reports, from the company's announcement, that Medical Microinstruments (MMI) raised $125 million in an oversubscribed Series D round (a late-stage private funding round) led by existing investor BioStar Capital, with Angelini Ventures and S3 Ventures joining. MMI says the money will widen sales of its Symani robot, which helps surgeons make very small, precise movements in operations on tiny blood vessels and nerves, and pay for studies including REMIND, which is testing only whether Symani is safe for microsurgery on neck lymph nodes in Alzheimer's patients; Mark Toland, chief executive of MMI, says the aim is "large-scale deployment".
notes: Medtech Insight (the pool outlet) is behind a login. Read Medical Device Network (url above) and Startupbusiness.it; both rest on MMI's announcement. Startupbusiness gives about 50 systems installed and 3,500 procedures; not repeated in the summary. Louie Cannon, founder and senior managing director of BioStar Capital, is quoted by Startupbusiness but not named in the entry.
